window.status: Last trim freed memory, next trim due
notes: The top of the screen shows physical memory in use, as a percentage and in gigabytes, read from the system once a second.
Under it, a graph of memory in use over time. Each trim is marked on the graph at the moment it ran. The graph is the SDK's chart control, fed from a bounded series the tool keeps in memory.
Trim now is the accent button. While a trim runs it is disabled and the status bar says a trim is running; a second press cannot start a second trim.

The last trim's result sits under the graph: what started it (Trim now, the interval or the threshold), how many processes were trimmed, how many were skipped, and how much memory came back, measured before and after.
Next scheduled trim reads from the Schedule setting: the seconds left in interval mode, a plain statement in threshold mode, Off when the tool only trims on demand.
Processes excluded shows the count from the Exclusions list and opens it from the Exclusions button.
window.cut: The AutoIt window had File and Help menus (`MemBoost.au3:708-742`), three stat groups with drawn progress bars and peak bars for committed memory and CPU (`:1148`, `:1160`), cached and kernel pool labels (`:1132-1144`), a status icon swapped with the load (`:1089`), a donate strip with hover icons and a donate dialog on exit (`:543-544`, `:1232-1245`, `:1770-1774`), a splash (`:664-683`), update and processing animations (`:416-417`), a minimise-to-tray flow with a tray menu (`:1805-1830`, `:1878`), an Escape hotkey that minimises (`:692`) and a topmost Preferences dialog of four tabs (`:1953`). None of these is in this window. The menus, splash, animations, donate strip, drawn bars and the committed, CPU and pool panels are cut; settings and About are the framework's pages. The tray icon is not part of the window and is decided in `docs/inventory.md`. Every cut is recorded in the plan with its reason.

readme.lead: MemBoost frees physical memory by trimming the working sets of running processes, and tells you what each trim gave back.
what: A trim asks Windows to shrink the working set of each running process, so pages a program is not using go back to the system. You can trim on demand, on a timer, or when memory use is high and still rising.

Windows refills working sets as programs run, so a trim is a one-off relief, not a permanent change. That is why MemBoost shows the result of every trim next to a graph of memory in use, and why there is nothing to undo.
readme.new_intro: The C++ version keeps what the AutoIt tool did and adds four things.
new: The Overview screen draws memory in use over time and marks every trim on it, so you can see whether a trim helped and for how long.
Every trim lists each process it trimmed or skipped, with the memory each one gave back, instead of a single count.
An exclusion list you can edit.
Games, virtual machines and audio tools can be left alone; the AutoIt tool had an exclusion list in its code that nothing could fill.
On a shared or locked-down machine you can limit trimming to the processes you name.

reference.note: The AutoIt tool is one 2,625-line script, `src/MemBoost.au3`, with its build descriptor `src/MemBoost.sni`. Its `local/` folder holds loose executables and logs, not a distribution zip; the two sound files it plays are `.mp3` paths that the `.sni` ship list (which names `.wav` files) never delivers.

plan.scope: The whole port: baseline, trim engine, window, graph, release
plan.goal: MemBoost ships as a complete, standalone C++ tool: it trims the working sets of running processes on demand, on an interval and on a high-and-rising memory threshold, skipping the same processes the AutoIt original skips, and reports for every trim what was trimmed, what was skipped and how much memory came back, with a graph of memory in use over time, an editable exclusion list and an only-list mode.
plan.current_state: Nothing exists in C++. The repository holds the AutoIt original under `reference/au3/` (`src/MemBoost.au3`, 2,625 lines; `src/MemBoost.ini`, 36 lines; `src/MemBoost.sni`, 65 lines, whose ship list names 13 files), the chosen identity under `brand/`, `DESIGN.md` with the Sidebar window, and the kits. The original trims every process except its own and any matching an exclusion array that nothing fills (`MemBoost.au3:469`, `:1563-1606`), by calling `_WinAPI_EmptyWorkingSet` and ignoring its result (`:1578`), reports only a processed count (`:1613`), starts a trim from a button or tray item, from a countdown (`:1682-1702`) or when load is above 90 and rising (`:1670`, `:1717-1731`), and already draws a memory graph that marks no trims (`:763`, `:1151`). It writes no log line for a trim. The SDK's framework and its chart control are planned in Resolute-SDK and not built; the plan sections that consume them wait on `sdk-framework`.
inputs: `reference/au3/src/MemBoost.au3`: the tool being ported, and `reference/au3/src/MemBoost.sni`, which lists what ships with it.
`reference/au3/shipped/Language/MemBoost/en.lng` and `reference/au3/shipped/MemBoost.ini`: the only language pack (UTF-16) and the settings file an installed copy carries.
`reference/au3/local/MemBoost_X64.exe`: the shipped build the baseline and the parity check run (untracked; there is no `dist/` folder).
outcome: `MemBoost.exe` trims with the same skip rules and the same three triggers as the AutoIt original, proven by the parity check, and every trim returns a measured result.
The Overview screen shows memory in use, its graph with each trim marked, Trim now and the last trim's result; the Processes, Exclusions and Schedule screens work behind it.
The Sidebar window of `DESIGN.md` works in light and dark at every scale, by keyboard alone, and the tool ships with its settings, packs, documents and update file.
plan.adjacency_rationale: The list is the Processes screen, reached from the first screen, where a person sees what a trim touched and skipped. Reporting and audit are the Activity section, one line per trim. Settings are the framework's pages. Permissions do not apply: a process the tool may not open is skipped and reported by name, so no action needs a right the user lacks. Reverse does not apply: a trim asks Windows to shrink working sets, which refill by themselves, so there is nothing to put back.
baseline_items: Start a fixture of helper processes that each hold a known amount of memory, run `reference/au3/local/MemBoost_X64.exe`, press Optimize Memory once, and record each helper's working set before and after, plus the processed count shown in the status line (`MemBoost.au3:1613`). Done when: `docs/baseline/trim-manual.json` lists every helper with its before and after working set and the count shown.

Set `AutoOptimize=2` with `AutoOptimizeSeconds=5` and then `AutoOptimize=1` in a copy of `reference/au3/shipped/MemBoost.ini`, run each mode against the fixture, and record when trims fired and what started them (`MemBoost.au3:1659-1714`). Done when: `docs/baseline/trim-timer.json` and `docs/baseline/trim-intelligent.json` record the trim times against the clock and the memory load that preceded each.

Repeat the manual trim with `ForceBehave=1` and a helper started above Normal priority. Done when: `docs/baseline/trim-forcebehave.json` shows the helper's priority before and after (`MemBoost.au3:1582-1587`).
inventory_items: Record the windows and controls in `docs/inventory.md`: the main window (`MemBoost.au3:702`), its menus (`:708-742`), the three buttons (`:980-986`), the stat groups and bars (`:1060-1160`), the graph (`:763`), the donate strip (`:543-544`), the splash (`:664-683`), the tray menu (`:1805-1830`) and the Preferences dialog (`:1953`) with its mode radios and interval list (`:1964-1971`). Done when: every control-creation call in the file is listed with its window and its verdict (a section of the new window, the framework, or cut).

Record the strings: the pack sections read, the English text hardcoded in the buttons (`:980-986`), the tray items (`:1811-1817`, including the name "Memory Booster"), the completion notification (`:1619`) and the mode radios (`:1966-1971`). Done when: every string names its pack key or says why it is hardcoded and what replaces it.

Record the behaviours: the trim loop (`:1518-1656`), the manual and automatic flag and its reset (`:1527-1532`, `:1654`), the three triggers, the warning counter (`:1163-1173`), the CPU sampling (`:1178`), the `ForceBehave` demotion (`:1582-1587`), the startup shortcut (`:2402-2410`), the own-process trim (`:1735-1741`), the `.mp3` sound paths (`:1169`, `:1624`) that the `.sni` never ships, the `ConsoleWrite("DEBUG:` lines and the comment at `:1577` that says idle processes while all are trimmed. Done when: every system call in the file is listed, and the two system changes (the startup shortcut and the priority demotion) each carry a reverse or an honest no-reverse statement.

Record settings, logging, update and the ship list: the eleven tool keys of `reference/au3/src/MemBoost.ini` (`AutoOptimize` to `StartMinimized`) with their defaults, the `.sni` `[Distribute]` list (the four `.ani` files and two `.wav` files among them) and the absence of any trim log. Done when: every `.ini` key and every shipped file is marked keep, cut or remapped.

engine.title: Working-Set Trim and Triggers
engine.intro: The tool's core: which processes are trimmed, the Windows call that trims them, what is skipped, the three ways a trim starts and the measurement that makes every trim report what it returned. The skip rules and the triggers are the AutoIt original's; the measurement is new, because the original reported only a count.
build: Write the trim, its skip rules and its result record in `src/core/Trim.cpp`. Done when: a trim of a helper process lowers its working set and returns a result naming it.

Write the three triggers and the memory measurement in `src/core/Triggers.cpp` and `src/core/Memory.cpp`. Done when: each trigger starts a trim under test and the result states the memory before and after.
items: Implement `TrimProcess` in `src/core/Trim.cpp`: open the process for quota and query rights, call `EmptyWorkingSet` (the call behind `_WinAPI_EmptyWorkingSet`, `MemBoost.au3:1578`) and return trimmed, or skipped with the reason when it cannot be opened. Done when: a test trims a helper process and its working set drops, and a protected process is returned as skipped by name. Cheaper substitute: ignoring the call's result as `MemBoost.au3:1578` does, which counts a process as trimmed that was never touched.

Implement `TrimAll` in `src/core/Trim.cpp`: take a snapshot of running processes, skip the tool's own process id (`MemBoost.au3:1565`) and any process whose name contains an entry of the exclusion list, case-insensitively (`:1569-1575`), and trim the rest. Done when: a test with three helpers and one excluded name leaves the excluded one untouched and reports the other two trimmed. Cheaper substitute: exact-name matching, which misses the versioned names the substring rule catches.

Measure each trim in `src/core/Memory.cpp` with `GetPerformanceInfo` (the source of `MemBoost.au3:1063`): physical memory in use is total minus available (`:1071`), read before the first process and after the last, with the duration. Done when: a test returns a `TrimResult` whose `freed` equals the difference of the two readings and whose duration is non-zero. Cheaper substitute: reading the free figure from an earlier sample, which credits the trim with whatever else moved.

Implement the manual trigger `TrimNow` in `src/core/Triggers.cpp` with the original's re-entry guard (`MemBoost.au3:1520`) and a record of what started the trim (manual or automatic, `:1527-1532`). Done when: two calls made while a trim runs start one trim, and the result names its trigger.

Implement the interval trigger in `src/core/Triggers.cpp`: a countdown that ticks once a second, pauses while a trim runs, trims at zero and restarts from the interval (`MemBoost.au3:1535-1537`, `:1682-1702`), with the interval choices `5` to `120` seconds of the Preferences list (`:1964`). Done when: a test on a fake clock with a 5 second interval fires at 5 and again at 10, and the countdown holds while a trim runs.

Implement the threshold trigger in `src/core/Triggers.cpp`: keep the last 10 load readings, and trim when the load is above 90 and the readings rose in at least 6 of the last 9 steps (`MemBoost.au3:1670`, `:1717-1731`). Done when: a test with a rising series above 90 trims once, and a flat series at 95 or a rising series at 85 does not.

Hold the trigger mode and the interval as settings in `src/core/Schedule.cpp` (off, interval or threshold; `AutoOptimize` and `AutoOptimizeSeconds` of `reference/au3/src/MemBoost.ini`, default interval 60 seconds) for the Schedule screen to read and write. Done when: a test sets each mode, restarts the engine and reads it back. Cheaper substitute: keeping the mode in a window control, which is lost when the window closes.

Implement the optional `ForceBehave` demotion in `src/core/Trim.cpp`: when set, lower a process above Normal priority to Normal (`MemBoost.au3:1582-1587`); it is off by default (`ForceBehave=0`) and the Schedule screen states that it is not undone. Done when: a test with a helper at above-normal priority sees it at Normal after a trim with the option on and unchanged with it off. Cheaper substitute: leaving the option out, which drops a documented behaviour of the original.

Cover the engine in `tests/trim_test.cpp` with helper processes the test starts and stops with their whole process tree on teardown and on timeout. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L trim` passes, and fails when the own-process skip or the exclusion rule is removed.
engine.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L trim` passes for the skip rules, the three triggers and the measured result, and fails when the own-process skip or the exclusion rule is removed.
engine.commit: core: working-set trim, three triggers, measured result

parity_items: Add `tests/fixtures/baseline/` as a copy step from `docs/baseline/` at configure time. Done when: the parity test reads the committed baseline and no path is typed into a tracked build file.

Compare which processes the engine trims, skips and demotes with the committed trim baselines, including the interval and threshold runs. Done when: the test covers `trim-manual.json`, `trim-timer.json`, `trim-intelligent.json` and `trim-forcebehave.json`, and the set of trimmed processes and the trigger times match.

enhancements.title: Editable Exclusion List
enhancements.intro: The AutoIt exclusion array exists and the trim loop honours it (`MemBoost.au3:469`, `:1569-1575`), but nothing ever fills it. This section makes it a list a person edits: add, remove and switch an entry on or off, with the substring rule kept. With an empty list a trim does exactly what the original does.

surface.fidelity: the Exclusions screen, against `DESIGN.md` section 2 and `sdk/DESIGN.md` section 16.
surface.job: a person protects games, virtual machines and audio tools from trimming once and trusts it afterwards. Consumer: the stored list and the skipped processes.
surface.treatment: the substring rule stated on the screen, each entry with an on and off switch, the list kept with the settings. Cheaper substitute that fails the checkpoint: exact-name matching, or a list the interval trigger ignores.

build: Write the list model in `src/core/ExclusionList.cpp`. Done when: add, remove and switch are tested and the list survives a restart.
Build the Exclusions screen in `src/ui/ExclusionsView.cpp`. Done when: an entry added there keeps a matching helper untouched in the next trim.
items: Implement the list in `src/core/ExclusionList.cpp` with entries of text and an enabled flag, matched as a case-insensitive substring of the process name as `MemBoost.au3:1570` does, stored through the framework's settings. Done when: a test adds two entries, switches one off, restarts and reads both back. Cheaper substitute: a private settings file written by the tool.

Pass the list into `TrimAll` for every trigger. Done when: a helper whose name matches an enabled entry survives a manual, an interval and a threshold trim untouched, and an unlisted helper is trimmed beside it.

Build `src/ui/ExclusionsView.cpp` from the SDK's list and toolbar controls: add, remove, a switch per row, and the rule written above the list. Done when: each row shows its entry and state in words, and the screen is operated by keyboard alone. Cheaper substitute: a text box holding a delimited string.
Show the empty state with one sentence, and update `Processes excluded` on the Overview screen. Done when: an empty list shows the sentence and None, and one entry changes the row to a count.
Prove non-interference. Done when: the parity check re-runs with the list empty and reports zero differing fields, and `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L exclusions` passes.
enhancements.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L exclusions` passes: a listed helper survives all three triggers beside a trimmed one, the list persists, and the empty-list parity run reports zero differences.
enhancements.commit: feature: an exclusion list a person can edit

enhancements.title: Per-Process Trim Report
enhancements.intro: The AutoIt tool reports a processed count and nothing else (`MemBoost.au3:1613`). This section reports each process: what was trimmed and how much it gave back, what was skipped and why (the tool itself, excluded, not on the only-list, could not be opened). Reads and display only: the trim is untouched.

surface.fidelity: the Processes screen, against `DESIGN.md` section 2 and `sdk/DESIGN.md` section 16.
surface.job: a person sees what a trim did instead of trusting a count. Consumer: the report and one Activity line per trim.
surface.treatment: one row per process with its working set before and after, the memory given back and, for a skipped one, the reason in words; totals under the list. Cheaper substitute that fails the checkpoint: totals taken from the system counter, which credits the trim with whatever else moved.

build: Measure each process before and after in `src/core/Trim.cpp`. Done when: a `TrimResult` carries one row per process with its figures or skip reason.
Show the rows in `src/ui/ProcessesView.cpp`. Done when: the screen after a trim lists every processed and skipped process.
items: Record in `src/core/Trim.cpp`, for each process, its working set before and after through `GetProcessMemoryInfo`, and its freed bytes; a skipped process records its reason. Done when: a test with a helper, an excluded helper and the tool's own process returns three rows, with the reasons named. Cheaper substitute: a single processed count.

Reconcile the rows with the total in `tests/report_test.cpp`: the freed bytes of the rows add up to the figure shown, and a process that grew is shown with its negative figure, not as zero. Done when: the test passes on a helper that allocates during the trim.

Write one Activity line per trim with its trigger, totals and duration, and keep the last report after the window closes. Done when: after a driven trim the Activity list shows the line and a restart shows the last report.

Build `src/ui/ProcessesView.cpp` from the SDK's list control, sortable by memory given back, with the totals beneath and an empty state before the first trim. Done when: the rows are read back through UI Automation and equal the `TrimResult`. Cheaper substitute: rows typed into the view, which show nothing real.
Prove non-interference. Done when: the parity check re-runs with zero differing fields and `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L report` passes.
enhancements.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L report` passes: the rows reconcile with the total, every skip has its reason, and the parity check still reports zero differences.
enhancements.commit: feature: a report of what each trim did to each process

enhancements.title: Only-List Trim Mode
enhancements.intro: The mirror of the exclusion list, for locked-down machines: when the only-list has entries, a trim touches the processes on it and nothing else. It is empty by default, so by default a trim does what the original does.

surface.fidelity: the only-list part of the Exclusions screen, against `DESIGN.md` section 2.
surface.job: an administrator confines trimming to approved processes on a shared or sensitive machine. Consumer: the stored list and the confined trim.
surface.treatment: a non-empty only-list wins over everything except the tool's own process, and the rule that an excluded process beats a listed one is written on the screen with the reason. Cheaper substitute that fails the checkpoint: an only-list that also trims unlisted processes sometimes, which makes the mode lie about its name.

build: Add the only-list to `src/core/ExclusionList.cpp` and to `TrimAll`. Done when: with two names on it a trim touches those two and no other.
Add its controls to `src/ui/ExclusionsView.cpp`. Done when: the list, its rule text and its empty state show on the screen.
items: Implement the only-list in `src/core/ExclusionList.cpp` with the same entry shape and substring rule, stored through the framework's settings. Done when: a test adds two entries and reads them back after a restart.

Make `TrimAll` trim a process only when the only-list is empty or matches it, with the tool's own process and exclusions still skipped first. Done when: a test with five helpers and two on the only-list trims exactly those two, and emptying the list trims all five again.

Report the skip reason `not on the only-list` through the trim report, and `excluded` for a process on both lists. Done when: a test with one helper on both lists returns it as skipped with the reason `excluded`.

Add the only-list to `src/ui/ExclusionsView.cpp` with the interaction rule written beside it. Done when: the rule text, the empty state and the list are reachable by keyboard and named to UI Automation. Cheaper substitute: a second text box with no rule shown, which leaves two lists fighting silently.
Cover it in `tests/onlylist_test.cpp`. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L onlylist` passes, and the parity check with the list empty reports zero differing fields.
enhancements.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L onlylist` passes: only listed processes trim, an empty list restores full trimming, and an excluded process on both lists is skipped with its reason shown.
enhancements.commit: feature: trim only the processes on an only-list

enhancements.title: Memory Graph
enhancements.intro: Asked for by the owner on 2026-11-15. The Overview screen draws physical memory in use over time and marks each trim on it. The graph is the SDK's chart control (planned in Resolute-SDK as `D01 T01 §5`, `shared/resolute-ui`), which is not built yet; the tool never draws its own graph. The tool samples memory into a bounded series held in memory and hands it to the control.

surface.fidelity: the graph on the Overview screen, against `DESIGN.md` section 2 and the chart control of `sdk/DESIGN.md`, in light and dark at 100 and 150 percent.
surface.job: a person sees whether memory use is climbing, whether a trim helped and how long the relief lasted. Consumer: the chart, read back against the series.
surface.treatment: a line of memory in use with a marker at each trim, labelled in words and readable without colour. Cheaper substitute that fails the checkpoint: a graph drawn by the tool itself, or one that shows no trim markers.

build: Write the bounded series in `src/core/MemorySeries.cpp`. Done when: a test adds more samples than its capacity and the oldest are dropped.
Bind the series and its trim markers to the SDK's chart control in `src/ui/OverviewView.cpp`. Done when: the Overview shows the graph with a marker for each trim.
items: Implement `MemorySeries` in `src/core/MemorySeries.cpp`: a ring of samples (time and memory in use) with a capacity declared once in `src/core/MemorySeries.h`, and a list of trim markers that drop out with the samples they point at. Done when: a test adds more samples than the capacity and the series holds only the newest, with no marker for a dropped sample.

Sample memory in use once a second through the measurement of `src/core/Memory.cpp`, as the original refreshes its stats (`MemBoost.au3:1018`, `:1151`), and add a marker when a trim ends, carrying its trigger and freed bytes. Done when: a driven trim leaves a marker at the sample taken after it. Cheaper substitute: sampling inside the window's paint, which stops when the window is hidden.

Bind the series to the SDK's chart control in `src/ui/OverviewView.cpp`, with the axis in percent of physical memory and a label on each marker. Done when: the control receives the series and the markers and the tool contains no graph-drawing code. Cheaper substitute: drawing the line with the tool's own paint code.

Make the graph readable without colour and by keyboard: the markers carry a shape and a text, and a focused marker announces its trigger and the memory it gave back. Done when: a UI Automation walk reads each marker's text and a keyboard path reaches them.

Capture the Overview in light and dark at 100 and 150 percent to `docs/captures/`, and cover the series in `tests/series_test.cpp`. Done when: four captures are committed, and `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L series` passes and fails when a trim marker is dropped.
enhancements.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L series` passes: the series stays within its capacity, each trim leaves a marker, and the Overview shows them through the SDK's chart control.
enhancements.commit: feature: a memory graph with each trim marked

plan.no_reverse: a trim asks Windows to shrink working sets, which refill by themselves as programs run; there is nothing to put back
verification: A walk of `reference/au3/src/MemBoost.au3` finds every piece in `docs/inventory.md` with its home.
The parity check reports zero differing fields against the shipped AutoIt build on the trim fixture, for the manual, interval and threshold runs.
